request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows the signed-in user's crew total in `my-crew-due-total`, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works:**
- A person counts as the user when their name or one of their aliases matches the user's name. Matching ignores case and surrounding spaces, the same way "My due" already works.
- The total is the due-totals of every crew such a person leads, added up. Each crew's due-total is worked out the same way as on its crew row: n/a figures are skipped.
- If no person with the user's name leads a crew, the field is blank.
- Someone who is in more than one of the user's crews is counted once for each crew, because the request says to add up the crew totals.

**Changes:** this was front-end only; nothing in the stored data, the server or the audit file changed.
- `features/crews/useCrews.ts`: a new shared `crewDues` helper that collects a crew's lead and member dues.
- `features/crews/crews.slot.tsx`: the crew row now uses that helper instead of its own inline version.
- `features/header/header.slot.tsx`: the new "My crew due" field.
